title: September DMI gave no clear added South Coast winter precipitation forecast gain in 1981-2026
abstract: We tested whether September Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index adds winter precipitation forecast value beyond July-September Nino 3.4. We used fixed HadISST1.1, ERSSTv5 and nClimDiv sources, with 46 South Coast California winter forecasts for 1981-2026. Each fit used earlier winters only. Adding DMI raised mean squared error by 4.45%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -10.40% to +1.84%. RMSE rose from 190.66 to 194.85 mm. All six planned settings had negative point gains and intervals that included zero. Individual score deletion left primary skill negative. These results give no clear added gain for this simple predictor. They do not show no Indian Ocean effect. Retrospective products, short records, model form and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval instructions. External source and record-level tables are excluded.

display.caption: Adding DMI gave negative point gains in six settings. Each conditional 95% five-year block interval includes zero.
